we have developed a statistical mechanics theory of linear manifold classification, which reveals the relation between the classification capacity and the manifold geometry, including the manifold radius, dimension, and label sparsity.

we have developed a statistical mechanical theory of the classification of general perceptual manifolds and that our theory provides a novel geometrical characterization of the classification capacity of general manifolds, as well as an explanation of the effects of label sparseness on classification capacity.

(i) a statistical mechanical theory of the linear classification of general manifolds is developed and applied to a number of representative examples including ellipsoids, polytopes, and orientation manfolds; and (ii) novel geometrical measures for manifolds are introduced and used to elucidate the classification capacity of general manifods.

the classification and geometry of perceptual manifolds, which are neural population response patterns to sensory stimuli associated with different physical attributes of the same object.
understanding how the brain classifies objects from the geometry of the manifold of neuronal responses to object features.

the geometry and topology of the manifolds play an important role in determining the classification capacity of the system, as well as the number of labels that can be reliably assigned to the manifold.
